records.claim: Scoreboard updates are triggered at instruction decode, execution completion, and instruction retirement/decoded tick.
records.quote: At decode, an instruction that writes a register stores its ROB index as a tag in the corresponding entry and clears the valid bit. When the instruction completes, we overwrite the payload with the digest of the produced value and set the valid bit.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly establishes decode, execution completion, and decoded instruction ticks as the operational trigger events.

records.claim: The on_decode routine marks the destination register entry invalid and initializes decay_ctr to 256.
records.why: Assigning decay_ctr = 256 collides with /state/0/entry_format and Table 3, which define decay_ctr as an 8-bit unsigned field whose maximum representable value is 255.

records.claim: The pseudocode invokes generate_digest(reg_type, value) to construct a 12-bit digest upon execution completion.
records.quote: Figure 6 shows the method we propose for generating digests of register values. RUNLTS generates a 12-bit digest from each 64-bit register value, with the format depending on the register type.
records.why: Section 4.2 defines generating a 12-bit digest parameterized by register type and value; the finding regarding 'digest(...)' is refuted as a substring match artifact.

records.claim: Aging decrements valid entries every decoded instruction and invalidates when the decay counter expires.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Section 4.2 states invalidation occurs after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, implemented via per-decoded-instruction decrements.

records.claim: Digest invalidation occurs after 256 decoded instructions to retain only fresh values.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Matches verbatim the motivation and 256-instruction lifetime described in Section 4.2.

records.claim: The scoreboard is an array of 65 entries corresponding to logical registers R0 through R64.
records.quote: We use a dedicated table that contains one entry per logical register.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Table 3 specify dedicated tracking for all 65 logical registers across 8 banks.

records.claim: Each scoreboard entry contains a 1-bit valid flag, a 14-bit payload for tag or digest, and an 8-bit decay counter.
records.quote: Each entry consists of a valid bit and a payload that can hold either a 14-bit tag or a 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Table 3 explicitly confirm the field widths { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) }.

records.claim: The register scoreboard tracking table consumes 1495 bits.
records.quote: { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65
records.why: Table 3 auxiliary data shows 65 entries times 23 bits per entry equals exactly 1495 bits.

records.claim: The scoreboard is directly indexed by logical register index 0 to 64.
records.quote: We use a dedicated table that contains one entry per logical register.
records.why: Section 4.2 defines one entry per logical register, corresponding to direct logical register indexing.

records.claim: Prediction Weight Tables consist of 8 banks, each containing tables WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), and WT2 (128 entries) with 6-bit weights.
records.why: Table 3 sR row confirms 8 banks containing tables of 128, 256, and 512 entries with 6-bit weights.

records.claim: Each prediction weight entry stores one 6-bit signed saturating weight in the range [-32, 31].
records.why: Table 3 defines the weight width as 6 bits, standardly interpreted as a signed [-32, 31] counter in SC components.

records.claim: The prediction weight tables consume 43008 bits in total.
records.why: Table 3 confirms 6 * (128 + 256 + 512) * 8 equals 43008 bits.

records.claim: Prediction weight tables are indexed by hashes combining branch PC and the selected 12-bit register digest.
records.quote: PC + reg. digest
records.why: Figure 5(c) shows the input to the hash generation for WT0, WT1, and WT2 is PC plus the selected register digest.

records.claim: The decay_threshold parameter default is 256.
records.why: A default value of 256 collides with /state/0/entry_format declaring decay_ctr as 8 bits (max 255). Lowering default to 255 resolves the contradiction while maintaining an 8-bit counter spanning 256 steps (255 down to 0).

records.claim: The tuning range for decay_threshold is [64, 1024].
records.open_question: The paper specifies invalidation after 256 instructions but does not evaluate or define an alternative tuning range for decay_threshold.

records.claim: Altering decay_threshold changes decay_ctr width by ceil(log2(decay_threshold)) bits per register.
records.quote: { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65
records.why: Table 3 demonstrates 8 bits per register are allocated for 256 steps where ceil(log2(256)) = 8.

records.claim: The default number of tracked registers is 65.
records.why: Table 3 explicitly specifies 65 tracked registers across UT and auxiliary storage tables.

records.claim: The tuning range for num_tracked_registers is [32, 128].
records.open_question: The paper fixes tracking to the 65 logical registers of the architecture and does not define a tuning range for num_tracked_registers.

records.claim: num_tracked_registers scales UT and scoreboard auxiliary storage linearly.
records.why: Table 3 calculates both UT storage and auxiliary scoreboard storage as direct linear multiples of 65.

records.claim: Integer register digest XOR-folds trailing zero count, leading zero count, and 6 LSBs into a 12-bit value.
records.quote: For integer registers, the digest encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits, effectively capturing characteristics of addresses and round numbers.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 6(a) define the exact XOR-folded layout tested by integer_digest_generation_check.

records.claim: Condition code flags replicate the 4 flag bits three times to form a 12-bit digest.
records.quote: For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 6(c) define 3x replication of 4 flag bits into 12 bits, matching flags_digest_generation_check.

records.claim: Advancing decode ticks decrements decay_ctr to 0 and clears the valid flag upon expiration.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Section 4.2 confirms that aging clears validity when the lifetime expires, verified by scoreboard_aging_invalidation.

records.claim: Positive bank usefulness scales the WT sum by 2.5 while non-useful banks contribute 0 to sR.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) shows per-bank scaling by x2.5 or suppression (x0) gated by bank usefulness, matching usefulness_gated_scaling.

records.claim: When multiple registers in a bank are valid, one is randomly selected during training to limit write ports to one.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update. Owing to this training method, each table in the register component also needs just a single write port.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly specifies random selection among available registers per bank to ensure single write ports.

records.claim: Predict (Lookup) is triggered at fetch / lookup time when computing Statistical Corrector inputs.
records.quote: Whenever the branch predictor queries the table, any entry whose valid bit is set forwards its digest to the register-value components in the SC for prediction.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that the register table forwards valid digests to the SC register components whenever the predictor queries the table.

records.claim: The lookup iterates across 8 register banks.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Section 4.2 establishes that the register component is partitioned into eight banks.

records.claim: In algorithm predict_sR, indexing UT at depth 4 with register variable r operates over the same register domain for bank b as chosen_reg in Update (Training).
records.quote: Each entry of the first table holds an eight- (or nine-) element vector of weights reflecting the usefulness of each register.
records.why: Section 4.2 establishes that each bank entry holds a vector of usefulness weights for the registers of that bank, so r and chosen_reg reference registers within the same bank domain.

records.claim: Usefulness is computed by summing weights from three 8-entry usefulness tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) indexed by skewed PC hashes.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies three 8-entry usefulness tables per bank indexed by PC.

records.claim: The register with the highest usefulness among available valid registers is selected.
records.quote: Unlike the existing components, this component picks the digest of the most useful register among those available and forwards it to the second table.
records.why: Section 4.2 specifies selecting the digest of the most useful available register within the bank.

records.claim: Prediction weights are looked up from three weight tables WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), and WT2 (128 entries) per bank.
records.quote: Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1", "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies WT0, WT1, and WT2 capacities as 512, 256, and 128 entries per bank.

records.claim: The bank weight sum is scaled by 2.5 when positive usefulness is detected, and masked with 0 otherwise.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) shows each bank's prediction weight sum feeding an output scaling stage of x0 or x2.5.

records.claim: Each entry in the Register Tracking Table contains a 1-bit valid flag, a 14-bit payload, and an 8-bit decay_ctr across 65 entries.
records.quote: { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65
records.why: Table 3 defines the auxiliary scoreboard state as 65 entries with valid (1), payload (14), and decay_ctr (8).

records.claim: The payload stores either a 14-bit ROB tag when invalid or a 12-bit register value digest when valid.
records.quote: Each entry consists of a valid bit and a payload that can hold either a 14-bit tag or a 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that the payload holds either a 14-bit tag or a 12-bit digest depending on whether the valid bit is clear or set.

records.claim: The Usefulness Weight Tables (UT) comprise 8 banks tracking 65 registers across three 8-entry tables per bank with 6-bit signed weights totaling 9360 bits.
records.why: Table 3 defines UT storage as 6-bit weights for 65 registers across three 2^3-entry tables, yielding 9360 bits.

records.claim: The Prediction Weight Tables (WT) consist of 8 banks each having three tables of 512, 256, and 128 entries with 6-bit weights totaling 43008 bits.
records.why: Table 3 specifies 8 banks of 128, 256, and 512 entries storing 6-bit weights totaling 43008 bits.

records.claim: The default number of register banks is 8.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly specifies that the component has eight banks.

records.claim: The default prediction weight table entry sizes are 512, 256, and 128 entries per bank.
records.quote: Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1", "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) labels the three prediction weight tables per bank as having 512, 256, and 128 entries.

records.claim: The default usefulness table entry count per table is 8.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) and Table 3 specify 8 entries per usefulness table.

records.claim: decay_threshold default value is 256, but decay_ctr is an 8-bit field with maximum representable value 255.
records.why: Section 4.2 specifies invalidation after 256 decoded instructions while Table 3 allocates an 8-bit decay_ctr (max value 255); an initial default of 255 provides 256 distinct count states (255 down to 0) to span 256 steps without exceeding the 8-bit field limit.

records.claim: bank_useful_multiplier default is 2.5.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) explicitly labels the bank output multiplier as 2.5.

records.claim: num_tracked_registers default is 65.
records.quote: { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65
records.why: Table 3 indicates 65 entries in the register tracking table.

records.claim: Integer register digests are formed by XORing trailing zeros/ones count, leading zeros/ones count shifted by 3, and the lowest 6 value bits shifted by 6.
records.quote: For integer registers, the digest encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 6(a) specify the 12-bit integer digest format by XORing the 6-bit trailing count, 6-bit leading count at bit 3, and 6-bit value slice at bit 6.

records.claim: Condition code flags digest replicates the 4 flag bits three times to form a 12-bit digest.
records.quote: For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 6(c) establish that condition-code flags replicate the 4 bits three times.

records.claim: Digests in the scoreboard decay with decoded instructions and invalidate when the decay counter expires.
records.quote: RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that digests are invalidated after subsequent instructions are decoded.

records.claim: A bank with positive usefulness scales its weight sum by 2.5, while an invalid or non-positive bank contributes 0.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies multiplying bank output by 2.5 when useful or 0 when not useful.

records.claim: When multiple registers are available in the same bank, one is randomly selected for updates to allow single-write-port tables.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update.
records.why: Section 4.2 describes randomly selecting one register among available ones in a bank during training.

records.claim: The algorithm is named 'Update (Training)'.
records.quote: During training, we update the correlations only for logical registers that were available at prediction time.
records.why: The paper explicitly discusses the training and update procedure for the register component.

records.claim: Training is triggered at Commit time (or Branch Resolution time).
records.why: The paper does not state whether sR training is triggered at instruction commit time or branch resolution time.
records.open_question: At which pipeline stage is sR training executed?

records.claim: Only one available register per bank is trained per branch event, chosen uniformly at random, so each table needs only a single write port.
records.quote: Owing to this training method, each table in the register component also needs just a single write port.
records.why: The paper confirms that random selection of a single register per bank ensures each table needs just one write port.

records.claim: Correlations are updated only for logical registers that were available at prediction time.
records.quote: During training, we update the correlations only for logical registers that were available at prediction time.
records.why: The paper directly specifies that only registers available at prediction time have their correlations updated during training.

records.claim: If several registers were available within the same bank, one of them is selected randomly for the update.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update.
records.why: The paper specifies random selection among available registers in a bank for the update.

records.claim: The update condition executes when sc_mispredicted is true or |LSUM| is within update_threshold.
records.quote: The predictor's operation remains almost the same as that of TAGE-SC-L.
records.why: RUNLTS uses the baseline TAGE-SC-L statistical corrector update rule, updating on misprediction or marginal confidence (|LSUM| <= update_threshold).

records.claim: Pseudocode contains an undefined helper call to confidence(...).
records.quote: The predictor's operation remains almost the same as that of TAGE-SC-L.
records.why: The token 'confidence' appears solely inside an explanatory comment and was falsely flagged as a function call by deterministic parsing.

records.claim: Pseudocode contains an undefined helper call to or(...).
records.quote: The predictor's operation remains almost the same as that of TAGE-SC-L.
records.why: The token 'or' is a standard boolean disjunction operator, not an undefined helper function.

records.claim: The usefulness weight (UT) of the chosen register is incremented if the bank's WT prediction direction matches the actual branch outcome, and decremented otherwise.
records.why: The paper does not detail the exact arithmetic condition under which UT usefulness weights are incremented or decremented.
records.open_question: What is the training update condition for usefulness table (UT) weights?

records.claim: UT is subscripted at depth 4 by chosen_reg (global logical register index 0 to 64) in Update (Training), whereas each bank's UT entry holds an 8- or 9-element vector indexed by bank-relative register index r.
records.why: Two statements in the spec collide: /state/1 declares that Bank b's UT entries contain an 8- or 9-weight vector for registers in that bank (indexed by bank-relative index r), but /algorithms/3/pseudocode subscripts UT at depth 4 with chosen_reg (0..64), which exceeds the entry vector bounds.

records.claim: The Register Tracking Table contains 65 entries corresponding to logical registers, each entry having 1 valid bit, 14 payload bits, and an 8-bit decay_ctr totaling 1495 bits.
records.quote: { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65
records.why: Table 3 auxiliary data explicitly defines the scoreboard structure as 65 entries of 1 valid bit, 14 payload bits, and 8 decay_ctr bits.

records.claim: The Usefulness Weight Tables (UT) comprise 8 banks with 3 tables of 8 entries each, storing 6-bit signed weights across 65 registers totaling 9360 bits.
records.why: Table 3 defines the UT capacity and entry organization matching 8 entries for 3 tables across 65 registers with 6-bit weights.

records.claim: The Prediction Weight Tables (WT) comprise 8 banks with 3 tables of 512, 256, and 128 entries of 6-bit signed weights totaling 43008 bits.
records.why: Table 3 defines the WT capacity across the 8 banks for sizes 128, 256, and 512 entries with 6-bit weights.

records.claim: The parameter num_banks has a default of 8.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that the register component is organized into eight banks.

records.claim: The parameter wt_entries has a default configuration of 512,256,128.
records.why: Table 3 and Figure 5(c) specify WT table sizes of 512, 256, and 128 entries per bank.

records.claim: The parameter ut_entries_per_table has a default of 8.
records.why: Table 3 and Figure 5(c) specify that each of the 3 UT tables per bank has 8 entries (2^3).

records.claim: The parameter decay_threshold default value is 256.
records.why: Two statements in the spec collide: Section 4.2 prose specifies invalidating digests after 256 instructions leading to default 256, but Table 3 allocates only 8 bits for decay_ctr declared in /state/0/entry_format (max value 255). Lowering default to 255 allows 256 states (0..255) to fit within the 8-bit counter.

records.claim: The parameter bank_useful_multiplier has a default value of 2.5.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) explicitly labels the bank usefulness multiplier stage as x0 or x2.5.

records.claim: The parameter num_tracked_registers has a default value of 65.
records.why: Table 3 confirms 65 logical registers tracked across the 8 banks.

records.claim: Integer register digest XOR-folds trailing count, leading count shifted by 3, and 6 LSBs shifted by 6 to yield 0x3E3 for value 0x8.
records.quote: For integer registers, the digest encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits, effectively capturing characteristics of addresses and round numbers.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 6(a) specify the exact XOR overlap of the 3 6-bit fields forming the 12-bit integer digest.

records.claim: Condition code flags value 0x9 replicated 3 times produces digest 0x999.
records.quote: For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 6(c) establish that flags are replicated three times into the 12-bit digest.

records.claim: Scoreboard aging invalidates a digest after decay_ctr reaches 0 upon decoding subsequent instructions.
records.quote: RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that digests are invalidated after subsequent instructions are decoded.

records.claim: Bank contribution is scaled by 2.5 when usefulness is positive and 0 otherwise.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) establishes the x0 or x2.5 scaling on bank usefulness.

records.claim: When multiple registers are available in a bank at prediction time, exactly one is randomly chosen for WT/UT table update.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update.
records.why: Section 4.2 dictates random selection of one available register per bank during training.
